title: Avatar Workshop
summary: Guess Who’s Talking. Attendees build a photoreal avatar that listens with Flux, thinks with Claude and lip-syncs through Anam, then play a mystery-guest game against each other. Runs in the browser on this site — nothing to install.
detail: Your microphone goes to Deepgram’s Voice Agent, which listens with Flux, thinks with Claude, and speaks. That speech drives an Anam avatar in audio-passthrough mode, so the face lip-syncs to it.
outcome: A talking avatar running on your own laptop that holds a live voice conversation in character, and a mystery-guest game you can play against a partner.
prereqs: Wired headphones, not speakers — on speakers the avatar talks to itself.
An Anam API key from lab.anam.ai.
A Deepgram API key from console.deepgram.com. New accounts get credit, no card needed.
artifact: A talking avatar in character, and a mystery-guest game the attendee plays with a partner.

flow.title: Run it here
flow.note: Nothing to install. Bring your own Anam and Deepgram keys, pick an avatar, and have a partner set the secret figure.

sections.title: Tech track — run it on your machine
sections.summary: Eight steps, about 45 minutes, most of it waiting on sign-ups. Nothing here is typed into an AI; you do every step yourself.

steps.title: Install Node.js
steps.instruction: Download the LTS build from nodejs.org and click through the installer with its defaults. Then open a terminal — Terminal on Mac, PowerShell on Windows — and run node -v.
steps.check: You see a version number starting v20 or higher. If it says command not found, close the terminal, reopen it and try again.

steps.title: Download the project
steps.instruction: On the repo page click the green Code button, then Download ZIP. Unzip it to your Desktop and rename the folder to exactly talking-avatar, because the later commands assume that name.
steps.check: The folder holds server.js, a public folder, a prompts folder, and a hidden .env.example. Press Cmd+Shift+. on Mac to reveal hidden files.

steps.title: Get your Anam key
steps.instruction: Sign in at lab.anam.ai, find API Keys in the left menu, create one named class, and copy it somewhere safe for a moment.
steps.check: You have an Anam key copied and ready to paste.

steps.title: Get your Deepgram key
steps.instruction: Sign in at console.deepgram.com, click API Keys, then Create a New API Key. Name it class and leave the permission as Member.
steps.check: You copied the key straight away — Deepgram shows it once. If you lose it, just make another.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.instruction: In the terminal run cd ~/Desktop/talking-avatar (Windows: cd $HOME\Desktop\talking-avatar), then npm install.
steps.check: You see roughly "added 80 packages" and a new node_modules folder. That takes under a minute.

steps.title: Start the app
steps.instruction: Run npm start and leave this terminal window open. The app runs only while it stays open.
steps.check: Four lines print, ending with the localhost:4400 address. If you see "Port 4400 is already in use", put PORT=4401 in .env.

steps.title: Open it and save your keys
steps.instruction: Go to http://localhost:4400 in Chrome and allow the microphone. In the first card on the right, paste the Anam key and the Deepgram key, then click Save keys.
steps.check: It says the keys were verified and written to .env, and the Avatar and Voice lists fill in. A rejected key usually means a stray space.

steps.title: Talk to it
steps.instruction: Headphones on. Pick an avatar and a voice, then have a partner type the Secret figure so you do not know it. Pick your microphone and check the green bar moves. Click Start conversation.
steps.check: The status turns green and says Listening, and the avatar greets you in character. Interrupting it is fine — it stops and listens.

sections.title: Non-tech track — build it in the Playground
sections.summary: Same character, same voice, nothing installed. Runs in the browser at playground.deepgram.com.

steps.title: Paste your key and check your audio
steps.instruction: Paste your Deepgram API key at the top of the Playground. Confirm the microphone is on and that you are on wired headphones rather than speakers.
steps.check: The Playground accepts the key and your microphone is selected.

steps.title: Write the persona
steps.instruction: Find the prompt box. This is where the agent gets its entire personality. Write the mystery-guest rules: stay in character, never volunteer the name, answer questions in the first person.
steps.check: The prompt names who the character is and states plainly that it must not reveal the name until it is guessed.

steps.title: Pick a voice and clear the greeting
steps.instruction: Choose a Flux voice, then delete the greeting message so the character opens in its own words instead of a canned line.
steps.check: No greeting text remains and a Flux voice is selected.

steps.title: Lower the temperature
steps.instruction: Set the temperature to somewhere between 0.3 and 0.5. Higher values wander off character during a guessing game.
steps.check: Temperature is in range and the character stays consistent across a few turns.

troubleshooting: The avatar talks to itself: you are on speakers. Switch to wired headphones.
Port 4400 is already in use: close whatever is using it, or set PORT=4401 in .env.
A key is rejected: it was pasted with extra whitespace, or it is the other service’s key.
No video: the avatar streams over WebRTC from Anam, so a weak network shows audio without a face.
The avatar appears but never speaks: check the voice is a Flux voice. Pairing Flux listening with an Aura voice connects cleanly and then produces no sound.
